Tramadol is implicated in the pathway as a target of both milnacipran and atomoxetine, which in turn target SHBG. This indicates that Tramadol may influence SHBG through the actions of these two drugs, which are themselves targets of Tramadol. The scores from the paths, though not directly measuring the strength of the Tramadol-SHBG relationship, suggest a plausible biological pathway where Tramadol indirectly affects SHBG via its interaction with milnacipran and atomoxetine. The evidence supports a mechanistic link, though the exact nature of Tramadol's role in this pathway remains unclear. The findings highlight the importance of considering drug-target interactions in understanding the broader pharmacological effects of Tramadol.
